overview.text: Houston is Texas’s largest city and a major urban center on the upper Gulf coastal plain, about 50 miles from the Gulf of Mexico. Its landscape includes an extensive network of bayous and canals. Founded in 1836 between White Oak and Buffalo Bayous, it was named for Sam Houston; its founders chose the site partly because they expected Buffalo Bayou to provide a shipping route toward the Gulf. Railroads and later the Houston Ship Channel and Port helped make Houston a major shipping and commercial center. The U.S. Census Bureau estimated 2,397,315 residents in 2025, ranking Houston fourth among U.S. cities and first in Texas.

key_facts.text: Houston lies on the upper Gulf coastal plain, about 50 miles from the Gulf of Mexico.
The city was founded in 1836 between White Oak and Buffalo Bayous and named for General Sam Houston.
Houston’s founders expected Buffalo Bayou to be a shipping route between the Gulf coast and inland Texas.
Railroad expansion helped Houston become a shipping center; the later Ship Channel and Port brought further commercial growth.
The Census Bureau estimated Houston’s population at 2,397,315 on July 1, 2025, making it the largest Texas city and fourth-largest U.S. city by population.
